chapter_theme: Seeing the guru of knowledge (ஞானகுரு தரிசனம்): the guru's state lies beyond the tattvas and the turiyas and cannot be spoken, yet to fix the mind on his form clears the three malams, as the thought of Garuda clears poison. Nandi as guru takes the seeker's head, mouth, eyes and mind, enters the heart, cuts the bonds and makes even the smallest great, until the disciple no longer bows to gods but becomes what others bow to.
structure_note: The guru's state beyond tattvas and turiyas (2656, 2657, 2661); what seeing him does (2658 to 2660, 2665); where and how he is found within (2662 to 2664, 2666 to 2671); the Lord's rule and grace in the world (2672, 2673); and Tirumular's own transformation (2674). The grouping is mine.

2656.reading: When the thirty-six subside there, the supreme guru grants what is to be worshipped, gives Siva's state above all else, and bliss swells and is kept as the gain.
2656.nuance: ஆறொடு முப்பதும் (six with thirty) is taken as the thirty-six tattvas. கும்பிடு தந்திடும் is unclear: the guru may give the act of worship, or give himself as the one to be worshipped.

2657.reading: The light that shines beyond the three turiyas, rare Parasiva, having become all things, in the ground left where expanding and contracting have ceased: the great guru's state cannot be spoken.
2657.nuance: துரியங்கள் மூன்றும் (the three turiyas) is traditionally the turiya of the soul, of the Shakti and of Siva, but the verse does not say. விரிவு குவிவு (expanding and contracting) may be the outward and inward movement of the mind or of the world.

2658.reading: I received my head for the feet of Nandi, my mouth to praise him, my eyes to see him, and my mind for him.
2658.nuance: Each line gives a part of the body its use. The epithets ஆயன, வாயன, காயன, சேயன rhyme and are hard to fix: perhaps 'who has become', 'who is in speech', 'who has a body' (the guru in visible form) and 'who is far'. The point is that the faculties were given for him.

2659.reading: As the heavy poison clears and fear ends as soon as one thinks of Garuda's form, so the moment one fixes on the guru's form the three malams clear and he becomes Siva.
2659.nuance: The image is of the snake-bite cure in which Garuda, the snakes' enemy, is held in mind. சிவன் அவன் ஆமே can mean the disciple becomes Siva, or that the guru is Siva; both readings are made.

2660.reading: No one knows where the Lord dwells; for those who search out his dwelling he settles within, never perishing, and if one sees the Lord, he becomes this one.
2660.nuance: அண்ணல் opens all four lines. அவன் இவன் ஆமே (he becomes this one) is the same turn as the close of 2659: the seer and the seen become one, which can be read either way round.

2661.reading: Knowing as things appear, appearing and not appearing, deluded knowledge, and the waking and the other states: these three go, and when the three turiyas end, Nandi stands fixed in the high silence.
2661.nuance: Which three are meant by மூன்றவை is unclear: the three kinds of knowing in lines 1 and 2, or waking, dream and sleep. மறி நனவாதிகள் may be the waking and the rest turned back. மோனம் here is the silent state of the guru.

2662.reading: In the land of the moon, between one's brows, in a fragrant flower, is the maiden of two petals, crystal-formed and free of bond; she is the hold of the supreme guru who cut the bonds.
2662.nuance: The two-petalled flower between the brows is traditionally the ajna centre, and the maiden there is taken as Shakti. சந்திர பூமி (the land of the moon) is a yogic term I can't fix. பற்று may mean that she is what the guru holds, or the refuge he gives.

2663.reading: He entered the mind so the seven worlds rejoiced, entered the earth bearing up the long sky, entered into wrath so the eight directions shook, and entered the forest: this is what is meant by 'his town is to the north'.
2663.nuance: The verse is obscure. The wrath may allude to Siva's angry deeds, the forest to the ascetic's retreat, and the northern town to Kailasa, or in a yogic reading to the crown of the head. Who 'he' is (the Lord or the guru) is not said.

2664.reading: The colours and the sheaths that are oneself draw near, bird and forest are fit to be called oneself, and if one stands in the sixteen-fold path, the ten parts that seemed oneself become something other.
2664.nuance: கோசம் is taken as the five sheaths of the self, சோடச மார்க்கம் as the path through sixteen kalas, and தசாங்கம் as ten parts or limbs. The bird and forest may be the soul in the body. I can't fix the argument; the verse seems to say that what one took for oneself is seen as other on the path.

2665.reading: Our great Nandi, who joins and knows no parting, stays and melts one within when his form is thought of; for those who can see the heart hidden in its source, hard karma swoons away here, within those who dissolve.
2665.nuance: கருவில் கரந்து may mean hidden in the source, or hidden in the womb, that is, in the body. அழிவார் அகத்தே is unclear: 'within those who are undone' or 'they perish within'.

2666.reading: One can reach our Lord of the tattvas: cutting and cutting the many bonds, seeking to stand firm and contemplating him beyond thought, one reaches him, and he himself is dharma.
2666.nuance: தத்துவன் is the Lord as the real, or as master of the tattvas. நினைப்பற உள்கில் (if one contemplates with thought gone) holds a paradox the chapter returns to. The last line may also mean that reaching him is itself dharma.

2667.reading: He thinks of those who think of him, he of the light of the flower that grows in the spring; even those as small as a split millet seed, if they reach him with a weighty mind, become high.
2667.nuance: The flower in the spring (சுனை) is commonly taken as the heart lotus. கனத்த மனம் may be a full, firm or devoted mind. The verse sets the measure of greatness in the mind's turning to him, not in one's station.

2668.reading: At the time of reaching him, if one sets aside the tattvas, take that too as the rule of attaining; those who think of the first Lord who stands as all the worlds will seek and find devotion.
2668.nuance: மேவை விதி is obscure, perhaps 'the rule for reaching'. பத்தி may be devotion, or, less likely, order. The verse seems to make letting go of the tattvas part of the method, not its failure.

2669.reading: Contemplating the Lord they ceased to waver; joined with our Lord they ceased from what happens; within their own minds they ceased from display; and he entered and stayed, showing the way of glory.
2669.nuance: The three ceasings are built on நகழ்வு, நிகழ்வு and திகழ்வு. நகழ்வு is an unusual word, taken here as wavering; திகழ்வு may be shining or display. The plain sense is a growing stillness ended by the Lord's entry.

2670.reading: Like a line of emerald and ruby that appears, the true path of the true guru of the great word joins; this line, at the root of the forehead, becomes the light within the beautiful light.
2670.nuance: இலாடம் is the forehead, and the line of green and red there is taken as a light seen between the brows in meditation, perhaps the meeting of Shakti and Siva. சந்திடு (joins) may describe the colours meeting or the disciple joining the path.

2671.reading: The yogic god dwells as the mouth that eats, the body, the life and the eye; he is earth, water, fire, air and sky, and the form of those who have become the open expanse is beyond even the sky.
2671.nuance: யோகக் கடவுள் may be Siva as yogi or the realised guru. The last line, வெளியானோர் மேனி, seems to say that the body of those who have become the void is no longer bound to the elements; the syntax is loose.

2672.reading: Proclaiming him Pasupati, Parasiva's command runs through the whole earth by its half; having made the great seat, he made the earth too a fitting seat for the devotees who come after.
2672.nuance: The verse plays on பதி as Lord and as dwelling place. பாதியால் (by the half) may refer to Shakti as Siva's half, through whom his command works. பின்னாம் அடியார் may be later devotees or those who follow.

2673.reading: Of the Lord of space, the wide earth and its long groves, they say: we know nothing but that they are his; the gods in heaven and the asuras did not see him, but those who received our Lord's grace remained in it.
2673.nuance: Line 2 is compressed: தம்பரம் அல்லது may be 'other than his supremacy' or 'other than his own'. The contrast between the gods who did not see and the graced who did is a common Saiva turn.

2674.reading: Taking the loincloth so that kings would bow, and then by Nandi's grace so that tongues would bow too, we will bow to gods no more: our mind is clear, and we have become what others go to worship.
2674.nuance: The verse puns: கோ வணங்கும் (kings bow) and கோவணம் (the loincloth), நா வணங்கும் (tongues bow), தே வணங்கோம் (we will not bow to gods). Whether the loincloth is Nandi's or the speaker's own renunciant garb is not said. The boast that the graced become an object of worship is strong and is offered as the fruit of the guru's grace.

links.note: 2940, in the chapter on the samadhi of silence, opens with the same line, the light shining beyond the three turiyas, and also speaks of expanding and contracting; here the state is the guru's and cannot be spoken, there it is a state of experience beyond speech.

The Kural calls a head that does not bow to the Lord's feet as useless as a sense that cannot perceive; Tirumular says the same from the other side, that his head, mouth, eyes and mind were given to him for Nandi.

Both make the small great by what they cling to: in the Naladiyar the hare is worshipped with the moon it lives in, so the slight gain worth by friendship with steady men; in Tirumular those as small as a split millet seed become high by reaching the Lord with a firm mind.

The Kural makes one's own deeds the touchstone of greatness and smallness; Tirumular names another measure, the mind that reaches the Lord, by which even the smallest become high. The two need not conflict, but the test differs.

2656 says that when the six and thirty subside (ஆறொடு முப்பதும் அங்கே அடங்கிடில்) the supreme guru gives Siva's state and bliss swells. Thiruppugazh 203 asks to reach the light of consciousness that lies beyond the six-times-six (ஆறாறின் அதிகம்) and beyond turiya, and to join with joy the unchanging Sthanu of bliss. Both place the goal past the thirty-six tattvas and name it as bliss; the Tirumanthiram says the guru gives it, the Thiruppugazh asks Murugan for it.

2659 says that as heavy poison clears as soon as one thinks of Garuda's form, so the three malams clear the moment one fixes on the guru's form (குருவின் உருவம் குறித்த அப்போதே திரிமலம் தீர்ந்து). 2409 uses the poison cure the other way: as poison once drawn out does not rise again (விட்ட விடம் ஏறாவாறு போல்), the one who has seen the truth does not return to the bond. Read together, the image covers both the speed of the cure and its permanence.

2660 says no one knows where the Lord dwells (அண்ணல் இருப்பிடம் ஆரும் அறிகிலர்), yet for those who search it out he settles within (உள்ளே அமர்ந்திடும்). 1722 says the Lord stood where nothing could know him, and yet he made the poet's body his temple (என்னுடல் கோயில்கொண்டானே). Both make the unknowable Lord a dweller in the seeker; 1722 names the dwelling as the body.

2661 says that when the three turiyas end (துரியங்கள் மூன்றற) Nandi stands fixed in the high silence (உயர்மோனத்தானே). 2159 places turiya within waking and ends that where turiya ceases cannot be told (துரியம் இறந்திடம் சொல்லஒண்ணாதே). Both put what lies past turiya beyond speech; 2661 names it as the guru's silence.

2663 lists the Lord entering the mind, the earth, wrath and the forest and ends: this is what is meant by 'his town is to the north' (ஊர் வடக்கென்பது ஆமே). 2070 says people say 'north, north' though nothing is placed there, and that for those who know, all the world in the north lies within (அகத்தில் அடங்கும்). 2070 gives the rule that 2663 applies: the northern dwelling is to be read inwardly.

2666 says that by cutting the many bonds and contemplating beyond thought one reaches the Lord of the tattvas, and he himself is dharma (தருமமும் தானே). Kural 8 calls the Lord whose feet one must reach a sea of dharma (அறவாழி அந்தணன்), without whom the other seas are hard to swim. Both make the Lord himself the dharma one reaches, not a giver of rules; the Tirumanthiram names bond-cutting as the way, the Kural reaching the feet.

2671 says the yogic god dwells as the mouth that eats, the body, the life and the eye, and as earth, water, fire, air and sky (மண்ணு நீரனல் காலொடு வானுமாய்). 2967 says he himself stands as the directions and the gods, and as body, life and tattvas (தானே உடலுயிர் தத்துவமாய் நிற்கும்). Both make the Lord the very constituents of the body and the world; 2671 adds that those who have become the open expanse go beyond even the sky.

2673 says the gods in heaven and the asuras did not see him (உம்பருள் வானவர் தானவர் கண்டிலர்), but those who received his grace remained in it. 1533 says those who saw all six sects did not see him (ஆறு சமயமும் கண்டவர் கண்டிலர்) and bids one become clear and settle. Both say the Lord is not seen by rank or by survey of doctrines; 2673 names grace as what does see, 1533 clarity.

2674 ends with Tirumular saying that, his mind made clear by Nandi's grace, he will bow to gods no more and has become what others go to worship (போய்வணங்கும் பொருளாயிருந்தோமே). Kural 268 says all other lives bow to the one who has wholly won his own self (தன்னுயிர் தான்அறப் பெற்றானை ஏனைய மன்னுயிர் எல்லாந் தொழும்). Both make the one who is inwardly won the object of others' worship; the Kural gives the cause as tapas, the Tirumanthiram as the guru's grace.

source_issues: 2657: line 1 is identical to 2940 line 1, and line 3 is close to 2940 line 3; one of the two may be a borrowing or a repeat.
2663 and 2664 are obscure throughout and may be corrupt; 2669 நகழ்வு is an unusual word.
